conventions.integers: All i64 values and time bounds are canonical decimal strings. No floating-point conversion.
conventions.typed_values: Values use str, bool or i64 tags. null appears only for an unbounded interval end or explicit event payload absence.
conventions.intervals: valid and known intervals are half-open [from,to). A null end means positive infinity. Known bounds are logical committed positions, not wall time.
conventions.cuts: Every case pins known_at. Point queries also pin valid_at. Interval queries declare from/to parameters.
conventions.events: Events and source IDs are immutable. semantics distinguishes business_event, assertion_change, and correction. A business reversal is another event.
conventions.projection: Each workload states how immutable events produce canonical EAV assertions. Assertions contain the normalized projected history; they are not extra input events.
conventions.results: expected_rows are typed set answers, independent of row order. Aggregate source identity is the complete typed source tuple or event ID as declared by the operation.
conventions.completeness: closed_fixture covers only the named domain and sources. Workload 10 additionally requires explicit event-time watermarks before concluding absence.
conventions.execution: These are fixture/oracle contracts. They contain no executed engine results, benchmark timings or claim that every operation has a native implementation.
conventions.knowledge_groups: Events sharing recorded_at belong to one fixture knowledge group. Runners must preserve grouped visibility at the declared cuts, including when mapping fixture positions to engine receipt positions.

workloads.title: Historical order status
workloads.projection: Status transitions supersede future valid-time status. Later knowledge retains earlier status intervals and the original earlier-knowledge assertion.

completeness.domain: order and ticks 0 through 40

workloads.title: Corrected customer address
workloads.projection: The correction closes the original assertion in knowledge time and asserts the backdated replacement. Both immutable arrival events remain.

completeness.domain: customer, address, ticks 0 through 20

workloads.title: Price at purchase
workloads.projection: Price events declare nonoverlapping price intervals. Purchase events remain immutable. Join each purchase timestamp to the price interval at the requested knowledge cut.

completeness.domain: product and purchases buy49/buy50; price history has no overlaps

workloads.title: Coverage at claim time
workloads.projection: Coverage is a half-open relation. Claim timestamps are immutable. The correction changes coverage knowledge without changing claim events.

completeness.domain: policy, customer and both claims

workloads.title: Duplicate and reordered webhooks
workloads.projection: Accept each source event ID once. Full object revisions reconstruct status intervals in authoritative revision order. The late older revision may fill earlier history but cannot replace newer state. Immutable accepted events remain distinct from deliveries.

completeness.domain: object, all four listed deliveries

workloads.title: Account balance
workloads.projection: Each distinct posting contributes its signed amount once in its currency. Reversal is a new posting and leaves the original immutable posting intact.

completeness.domain: account and all listed posting IDs

workloads.title: Available inventory
workloads.projection: Physical stock is the sum of physical deltas. Reserved stock is the sum of reservation deltas. Available equals physical minus reserved; releases never add physical units.

completeness.domain: sku and all physical/reservation movements

workloads.title: Net revenue by customer
workloads.projection: Sum each capture once and each distinct refund once before joining customer totals. Refund amounts are positive deductions and immutable refund events.

completeness.domain: customer, capture and both refunds

workloads.title: Paid but unprovisioned subscriptions
workloads.projection: Payment events contribute a paid subscription from occurrence onward. Entitlement validity is independent. Return paid subscriptions with no active entitlement at the same two-time cut.

completeness.domain: subscription S, with absence evaluated only at each requested knowledge cut

workloads.title: Stuck workflow with source completeness
workloads.projection: A watermark T certifies terminal events with occurrence strictly before T. Missing terminal knowledge is pending until watermark reaches the deadline. Missing completion at/after deadline then is overdue. A later completion remains a business event.

completeness.domain: W; terminal-feed completeness is watermark-gated, never inferred from an empty relation

workloads.title: Inherited access
workloads.projection: Follow transitive member_of edges to principals, then can_read grants on the resource or its ancestors. All supporting edges must be active at one shared cut. Duplicate identical grant assertions do not duplicate authorization answers.

completeness.domain: listed user/principals/document; full reachable principal/resource closure included

workloads.title: Explicit deny over inherited access
workloads.projection: An active user/resource block overrides every allow path. The correction removes erroneous block knowledge. Removing one of two independent grants leaves the other allow path.

completeness.domain: user and document, both grant paths and complete block source

workloads.title: Nested pallet contents
workloads.projection: Return leaf items reached through contains edges. The pallet/tray/case diamond gives duplicate paths to each item. Moving B changes valid containment from tick 10 while preserving earlier knowledge.

completeness.domain: listed containers/items and their complete descendant closure

workloads.title: Product recall
workloads.projection: Follow input_of transitively from contaminated lots, then collect customers of resulting shipped lots. Correcting the erroneous input edge removes the implication and retains the immutable shipment.

completeness.domain: A, clean, B and every shipment of B

workloads.title: Vulnerable deployed dependencies
workloads.projection: Traverse depends_on with visited tuple semantics. The diamond and Y/Z cycle yield one affected deployment, regardless of path count. Vulnerability is active only on its interval.

completeness.domain: X deployment and complete transitive dependency graph

workloads.title: Historical data lineage
workloads.projection: Run R outputs D at code version 7. Later input metadata is additive and preserves A/B. Resolve lineage using the requested knowledge cut, retaining the original run event.

completeness.domain: R, D and all input/code declarations

workloads.title: Ordered conversion funnel
workloads.projection: Qualify a session if it has event times view < checkout < payment, all within the half-open query window. Event arrival order and equal timestamps do not establish sequence.

completeness.domain: S, T, U and equal; every event in windows [0,41)

workloads.title: Machine uptime interval union
workloads.projection: Measure the union of visible up intervals clipped to the requested window. Duplicate observations and overlap add no duration. A later bridging interval fills the original gap.

completeness.domain: M and every interval intersecting [0,12)

workloads.title: Point-in-time ML features and labels
workloads.projection: Feature valid time is predicted_at and feature knowledge time is the prediction-recorded feature_known_at. Labels use the query knowledge cut. Completed examples require a known label. Later feature restatement is a distinct query.

completeness.domain: customer balance intervals, prediction P and its outcome label

workloads.title: Incremental alternate support
workloads.projection: Answers are sets. For this acyclic fixture, support count is the number of distinct node-sequence paths. Removing B>D leaves the C path; removing C>D removes the answer. A maintained view must equal full recomputation at each cut.

completeness.domain: A/B/C/D, both paths and all edge removals
